question_text: A dispersion-strengthened aluminum contains 10 vol $\% \mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$. Assuming that the metal phase is essentially pure aluminum, calculate the density of the composite. (The density of $\mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ is $3.97 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$.). Assume the density of pure aluminum is $2.70 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^3$.The unit of the answer is Mg/m^3.
response:
The composite density is the volume-fraction-weighted sum of the constituent densities:

$$\rho_c = V_{\text{Al}}\rho_{\text{Al}} + V_{\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3}\rho_{\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3} = 0.90(2.70) + 0.10(3.97) = 2.43 + 0.397 = 2.827 \ \text{Mg/m}^3$$

$$\boxed{2.827}$$
